intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the spectacular wildebeest migration across the Mara River, one of nature's greatest wildlife spectacles. Game drives through the Maasai Mara ecosystem offer sightings of the Big Five, cheetahs, and thousands of wildebeest and zebras crossing crocodile-infested waters. A shared group safari keeps costs manageable while delivering an unforgettable experience.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Game drives reveal lions, buffalo, and hundreds of elephants roaming the open savannah. The dramatic scenery and photographic opportunities are unmatched anywhere in Kenya.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park
experiences.description: Hike or cycle through Hell's Gate, one of Kenya's few parks where you can walk freely among wildlife including zebras, giraffes, and buffalo. Explore dramatic gorges, geothermal hot springs, and towering volcanic cliffs. A guided walking tour through the gorge includes natural hot spring pools for a refreshing dip in nature.

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Spend an evening with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara, learning about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and deep connection to wildlife and land. Participate in traditional dances, visit a boma (homestead), and enjoy a bush dinner under the stars with storytelling around a campfire. A deeply authentic cultural and nature immersion.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Visit Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its vast flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, along with leopards and Rothschild giraffes. A full-day game drive offers incredible birdwatching and rare rhino sightings in a stunning Rift Valley setting.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from a 24-hour airport kiosk or hotel reception upon arrival - budget around KES 300-500 (~$2-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange an airport transfer or use a reputable taxi app like Little Cab or Uber Kenya to keep costs low. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is late night. Keep your first night simple - rest is key for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a walk along the beachfront to get your bearings, enjoy the warm 25°C weather, and soak in the coastal atmosphere. Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby local market or town center for an authentic Kenyan experience. Browse fresh produce, local crafts, and street food stalls. This is a great opportunity to pick up snacks and water for the coming days at budget prices.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset stroll along the beach. Watch local fishermen bring in their catch. Dine at a local beachside restaurant near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or visit a local 'mama mboga' roadside stall for mandazi (fried dough) and chai tea - budget KES 100-150 (~$0.75-1.20 USD)
meals.lunch: Local market street food - try nyama choma (grilled meat) or a rice and beans plate at a local canteen - budget KES 300-500 (~$2-4 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachside local restaurant - try grilled tilapia or pilau rice with coconut fish stew - budget KES 500-800 (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: July is dry season in Kenya with warm weather and minimal rain (only 30mm expected for the month), making it ideal for outdoor exploration. Stay hydrated and use sunscreen. Exchange currency at a local bank or licensed bureau de change for the best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the coastal forest or mangrove area near the resort. Kenya's coast is rich in bird species. Bring binoculars if available - this is a free wildlife experience right from your doorstep. Look out for kingfishers, herons, and sunbirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby nature reserve or coastal marine park. Many coastal areas in Kenya offer affordable entry fees for budget travelers. Explore tide pools, coral reef viewpoints, and coastal vegetation. Look out for monkeys, monitor lizards, and shore birds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local dhow harbor if nearby to watch traditional fishing boats. Enjoy the warm evening breeze on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast using market items from yesterday - fresh tropical fruit (mango, papaya, passion fruit) and bread - budget KES 150-200 (~$1.20-1.60 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from the local market - samosas, boiled eggs, and fresh juice - budget KES 250-400 (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Try a local Swahili restaurant for authentic coastal cuisine - coconut rice (wali wa nazi) with fish curry - budget KES 500-700 (~$4-5.50 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Bring insect repellent for morning walks near mangroves. Check local marine park entry fees in advance - many are affordable at KES 200-500 for residents and budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip preparation - pack essentials and head out early for a full-day nature excursion. Visit a local wildlife sanctuary or conservation area accessible from the coast. Many areas offer guided walks with local rangers at affordable community rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wildlife sanctuary visit. Look for bush babies, colobus monkeys, and various antelope species. Participate in a guided nature walk to learn about local flora and fauna from a knowledgeable community guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Relax on the beach as the sun sets. Share stories with fellow budget travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early morning - local tea house or hotel breakfast - ugali with eggs or porridge - budget KES 150-250 (~$1.20-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from local market or canteen near the sanctuary - rice, beans, and vegetables (githeri) - budget KES 250-400 (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using fresh market ingredients if your accommodation has a kitchen, or dine at a budget local restaurant - budget KES 400-600 (~$3-4.80 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book guided walks through community-based tourism organizations for the most affordable and authentic experiences. These also ensure your money goes directly to local communities. Carry plenty of water and a light rain jacket just in case, even though rain is minimal in July.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day - take an early morning bus or matatu (shared minibus) to the nearest major wildlife area or national park. Matatus are the most budget-friendly way to travel in Kenya. Enjoy the scenic countryside views during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the national park or wildlife reserve. Check into budget camping or a budget guesthouse near the park entrance. Many parks have affordable public campsites at KES 500-1000 per night. Freshen up and prepare for wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Evening game drive or guided walk around the park perimeter. Watch wildlife come to watering holes at dusk - this is prime time for elephant, zebra, and giraffe sightings. Enjoy a campfire dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Quick roadside breakfast before boarding the matatu - mandazi and chai - budget KES 100-150 (~$0.75-1.20 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop lunch during travel - local canteen meal - budget KES 200-350 (~$1.60-2.80 USD)
meals.dinner: Campsite self-cooked meal or budget park lodge restaurant - ugali, sukuma wiki (kale), and beans - budget KES 400-600 (~$3-4.80 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book park entry fees in advance online through the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) website to save time. Budget for park entry: approximately KES 1,500-3,500 for non-residents depending on the park. Matatu fares vary by distance - confirm routes and prices at the bus station.

day_by_day.morning: Full day game drive in the national park. Start at dawn (around 6:00 AM) when animals are most active. Look for the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. July is excellent for wildlife viewing as vegetation is lower and animals congregate near water sources.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue game drive through different park zones. Visit a hippo pool or crocodile-filled river crossing if available. Take time to photograph giraffes, zebras, and wildebeest grazing on the savanna.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 6:30 PM (park rules). Enjoy a campfire dinner. Listen to the sounds of the African bush at night - hyenas calling, lions roaring in the distance. Stargaze in the clear July sky.

meals.breakfast: Early camp breakfast - packed bread, peanut butter, and fruit - budget KES 150-200 (~$1.20-1.60 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten in the vehicle during game drive - sandwiches, fruit, and water - budget KES 200-300 (~$1.60-2.40 USD)
meals.dinner: Campfire meal - rice and lentil stew or beans - budget KES 300-500 (~$2.40-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a self-drive vehicle or join a shared game drive with other budget travelers to split costs - this can reduce expenses significantly. Always follow park rules: stay in the vehicle, do not feed animals, and respect speed limits. Carry binoculars for better wildlife viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk with a KWS ranger around the park boundary or a designated walking safari zone. Walking safaris offer an intimate ground-level experience with wildlife and are often more affordable than vehicle game drives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the park's education or visitor center to learn about Kenya's conservation efforts, anti-poaching initiatives, and local ecosystems. Many centers are free or charge a nominal fee. Rest during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner experience - find a scenic viewpoint to watch the sunset over the savanna. The golden hour light on the African landscape is spectacular. Prepare a simple dinner at camp and enjoy the peaceful evening.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast - porridge with honey and fresh fruit - budget KES 150-200 (~$1.20-1.60 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp or visitor center canteen - chapati and vegetables - budget KES 200-350 (~$1.60-2.80 USD)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner - pasta with tomato sauce and local vegetables - budget KES 300-450 (~$2.40-3.60 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Walking safari fees vary by park - budget KES 500-1,500 for a guided walk. Always walk with a certified KWS ranger for safety. This is a great day to interact with rangers and learn fascinating facts about wildlife conservation in Kenya.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final game drive before checkout. Focus on areas you haven't explored yet. Look for cheetahs and leopards which are more active in the early morning. Take final photographs and cherish the last moments in the bush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the park campsite and travel back toward the coast or a different natural attraction. Stop at a roadside viewpoint or scenic area along the route. Visit a local Maasai or community cultural village if en route - many offer affordable entry fees and authentic cultural experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort or a budget guesthouse near the coast. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxing evening by the beach after days in the bush.

meals.breakfast: Quick camp breakfast before departure - bread, fruit, and tea - budget KES 150-200 (~$1.20-1.60 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant during travel - nyama choma or fish and chips - budget KES 350-500 (~$2.80-4 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebrate your safari experience at a local beachfront restaurant - fresh grilled seafood or Swahili pilau - budget KES 600-900 (~$4.80-7.20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: A Maasai cultural village visit typically costs KES 500-1,500 per person and includes traditional dances, village tour, and craft demonstrations. Always negotiate respectfully and purchase crafts directly from artisans to support local livelihoods. Budget for a small souvenir if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxing morning at the beach resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast and take a morning swim in the warm Indian Ocean. The July weather at 25°C is perfect for beach activities. Explore the reef at low tide for free snorkeling or wade through tide pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby nature trail or coastal forest for a final wildlife experience. Look for butterflies, coastal birds, and small mammals. Alternatively, visit a local botanical garden or nature center to learn about Kenya's coastal ecosystems and plant life.
day_by_day.evening: Souvenir shopping at the local market - look for handmade items like kikoi fabric, wooden carvings, and beaded jewelry. Support local artisans by buying directly. Enjoy a farewell dinner at your favorite local restaurant from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort or guesthouse breakfast - fresh tropical fruit platter, eggs, and coffee - budget KES 200-300 (~$1.60-2.40 USD)
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch - grilled fish, coconut rice, and fresh lime juice - budget KES 400-600 (~$3.20-4.80 USD)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered - treat yourself slightly - budget KES 700-1,000 (~$5.60-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: When souvenir shopping, bargaining is expected and culturally acceptable. Start at about 50% of the asking price and meet in the middle. Avoid buying items made from wildlife products (ivory, shells, certain feathers) as these are illegal to export and harm conservation efforts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya. Wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a peaceful walk along the shoreline to reflect on your incredible 10-day adventure. Pack your bags and check out of the resort, storing luggage if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy any last-minute activities near the resort - a final swim, a cup of Kenyan chai at a local cafe, or a visit to any missed local attraction. Head to the airport with plenty of time to spare.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before your international flight. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Kenyan coffee or tea as gifts. Board your flight with wonderful memories of Kenya's wildlife and nature.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast - mandazi, chai, and fresh fruit - budget KES 150-200 (~$1.20-1.60 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or at the airport - budget KES 300-500 (~$2.40-4 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the flight - budget KES 500-800 (~$4-6.40 USD) or included with flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight details and airport transfer arrangements the night before. Kenya's airports can be busy so allow extra time for security and check-in. Consider purchasing vacuum-packed Kenyan coffee or tea at the airport as affordable and lightweight souvenirs. Total estimated daily budget excluding park fees: KES 1,500-3,000 ($12-24 USD) per day for food and local transport.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid stress on arrival. Keep essentials in carry-on for the late-night check-in. The resort front desk should be notified of your late arrival ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront to recover from jet lag and acclimate to the warm Kenyan summer weather (~25°C). Explore the resort grounds and nearby coastal area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local nature reserve or coastal wetland near the resort for a gentle introductory wildlife walk. Spot local bird species and coastal flora. This low-key start helps ease into the trip before more intensive safari days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Browse the menu for fresh Kenyan coastal cuisine including grilled fish and local vegetables.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – included or mid-range resort rate
meals.lunch: Light meal at the resort's poolside café – grilled chicken wrap or fresh fruit plate (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant at the resort – grilled tilapia or coastal seafood platter with ugali (~$20–30)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery day. Hydrate well, apply sunscreen, and rest. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings and transfers with your tour operator today.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by road or domestic flight to Amboseli National Park. Check into a mid-range safari camp near the park. After settling in, enjoy a morning game drive through Amboseli's open plains with stunning views of Mount Kilimanjaro as the backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views – explore the park's famous elephant herds, some of Africa's largest, roaming freely against the iconic snow-capped peak. Look out for buffalo, zebra, wildebeest, and diverse birdlife around the swamp areas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for sundowners on the veranda. Enjoy a campfire dinner under the stars at the lodge's outdoor dining area with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or quick bite at resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed bush lunch provided by safari camp, enjoyed in the field during the game drive
meals.dinner: Three-course set dinner at the Amboseli safari camp lodge (~$25–35 per person or included in package)

day_by_day.notes: July is peak season at Amboseli – book safari camp well in advance. Morning light is best for Kilimanjaro views as clouds often gather by afternoon. Bring binoculars and a good camera with a zoom lens.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive in Amboseli National Park. This is the golden hour for wildlife photography and elephant sightings near the Ol Tukai swamp area. Watch for predators like lions and cheetahs in the early light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Amboseli's diverse ecosystems – open savanna, acacia woodlands, and marshlands. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic view of the entire park and the Kilimanjaro horizon. Spot hippos and crocodiles in the water channels.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Amboseli and transfer to Hell's Gate area near Naivasha. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or eco-lodge near Lake Naivasha. Enjoy a quiet dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full English breakfast at the Amboseli camp before the morning drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp or roadside stop en route to Naivasha – nyama choma (grilled meat) and chapati (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Naivasha eco-lodge or nearby local restaurant – lamb stew with rice and kachumbari salad (~$15–20)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Amboseli to Naivasha takes approximately 3–4 hours. Alternatively, consider a domestic flight to Nairobi and then a 1.5-hour drive to Naivasha to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park – one of Kenya's unique parks where you can walk or cycle freely among wildlife including zebra, giraffe, buffalo, and baboons. Hike through the dramatic gorge carved by ancient volcanic activity and hot springs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hell's Gate's gorge trails and Fischer's Tower rock formation. Visit the geothermal spa pools for a relaxing soak in natural hot springs after the hike. The 30mm monthly rainfall means occasional light showers – bring a light rain jacket.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lake Naivasha area for a sunset boat ride on the lake. Spot hippos, fish eagles, pelicans, and hundreds of bird species along the papyrus-lined shores.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Naivasha lodge – eggs, toast, fresh tropical fruit (~included or $8–12)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or picnic in Hell's Gate Park – sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Dinner at a lakeside restaurant in Naivasha – fresh Nile perch fillet with vegetables and ugali (~$18–25)

day_by_day.notes: Rent bicycles at the Hell's Gate gate for approximately $5–10 for a more immersive experience. Start early to beat the midday heat. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for the gorge walk.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 1 hour from Naivasha). Begin a morning game drive to spot the park's famous white rhinos and black rhinos in their sanctuary habitat. Lake Nakuru is one of the best places in Africa for rhino sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit – witness thousands of pink flamingos lining the alkaline lake shores in a breathtaking natural spectacle. Also watch for lions, leopards, Rothschild giraffes, and waterbuck. Visit Baboon Cliff viewpoint for panoramic lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range lodge inside or near Lake Nakuru National Park. Enjoy a peaceful evening with sundowners overlooking the lake, followed by dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Naivasha lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the park or at the lodge's picnic area
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nakuru lodge – three-course meal with Kenyan-inspired dishes (~$22–30)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. July is a great time for flamingo viewing. Carry your park entry fees – a mid-range budget should account for ~$60 per person per day for conservancy fees.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park focusing on the forested areas for leopard sightings and the southern sector for lion prides. The cool early morning is ideal for active predator behavior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lake Nakuru and drive to the Maasai Mara region (approximately 4–5 hours). Check into a mid-range tented camp on the Mara ecosystem outskirts. Freshen up and take a short afternoon game drive to get oriented with the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner – spend the evening with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara. Watch traditional dances, learn about Maasai customs, beadwork, and warrior culture, then enjoy a memorable bush dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Nakuru lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop en route to the Mara – local Kenyan restaurant serving pilau rice and beans (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Traditional bush dinner included in the Maasai Cultural Village Experience – roasted meats, maize, and local vegetables

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Cultural Experience typically costs $30–50 per person and is a highlight of any Kenya trip. Respect cultural protocols, ask before photographing community members, and bring small gifts like school supplies if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in the Maasai Mara – the prime time to witness the Great Migration action. July is peak migration season with massive wildebeest and zebra herds flooding the Mara from Tanzania's Serengeti. Watch for dramatic predator interactions at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari – position at the Mara River crossing points to witness the spectacular wildebeest river crossings, one of nature's greatest wildlife events. Crocodiles, lions, and hyenas await the crossing herds in an intense natural drama.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a well-earned rest. Enjoy a campfire dinner at the tented camp with other safari guests, sharing the day's incredible sightings. A guided night walk or spotlight drive may be available through the camp.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-drive packed breakfast or hot flask of tea and snacks in the vehicle
meals.lunch: Bush lunch in the Mara – packed meal enjoyed in the field with views of the migrating herds
meals.dinner: Campfire dinner at the Mara tented camp – BBQ meats, roasted vegetables, and local stew (~included in camp package or $25–35)

day_by_day.notes: July is the absolute best time for the Great Migration river crossings. Patience is key at crossing points – crossings can take hours to begin. Stay with a reputable guide and never pressure wildlife. Bring a dust cover for your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day deep Maasai Mara game drive. Explore the Mara Triangle and Ol Kinyei Conservancy areas for off-the-beaten-path wildlife encounters. Search for the Big Five – lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino – in the golden savanna grasslands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the Mara's open plains tracking cheetah families and large elephant herds. Visit the Mara River banks again for any afternoon migration crossings. The warm 25°C weather keeps wildlife active throughout the day.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on a scenic Mara hilltop with panoramic views across the golden savanna. Return to camp for a farewell dinner at the Mara tented camp, celebrating the incredible wildlife experiences of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the tented camp before the full-day drive
meals.lunch: Extended bush picnic lunch in the field – sandwiches, salads, fresh fruit, and cold drinks provided by camp
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the Mara camp – three-course meal with wine or local Tusker beer (~$30–40)

day_by_day.notes: Consider an optional hot air balloon safari over the Mara at dawn (~$450–500 per person) for a once-in-a-lifetime aerial view of the migration – book well in advance. This is the last full safari day so make the most of every moment.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara for last wildlife sightings and photography. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast and pack up. Depart the Mara by road or domestic flight back toward Nairobi or the coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by domestic flight). If time allows, visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre or David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage for a meaningful wildlife conservation experience close to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort or transfer to Nairobi for final night stay. Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner at a quality Nairobi restaurant or back at the resort, reflecting on 10 incredible days of Kenyan wildlife and nature.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast at the Mara tented camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi at a mid-range restaurant – Carnivore Restaurant for the iconic Kenyan experience or a local nyama choma joint (~$20–30)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality Nairobi restaurant or resort – Swahili coastal cuisine with fresh seafood and coconut rice (~$25–40)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and allow ample time for Nairobi traffic, which can be heavy especially on Friday afternoons. Purchase last-minute Kenyan souvenirs at the Maasai Market in Nairobi. Depart with unforgettable memories of Kenya's extraordinary wildlife.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Game drives reveal lions, buffalo, and hundreds of elephants roaming the open savannah. The dramatic scenery and photographic opportunities are unmatched anywhere in Kenya.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park
experiences.description: Hike or cycle through Hell's Gate, one of Kenya's few parks where you can walk freely among wildlife including zebras, giraffes, and buffalo. Explore dramatic gorges, geothermal hot springs, and towering volcanic cliffs. A guided walking tour through the gorge includes natural hot spring pools for a refreshing dip in nature.

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Spend an evening with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara, learning about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and deep connection to wildlife and land. Participate in traditional dances, visit a boma (homestead), and enjoy a bush dinner under the stars with storytelling around a campfire. A deeply authentic cultural and nature immersion.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Visit Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its vast flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, along with leopards and Rothschild giraffes. A full-day game drive offers incredible birdwatching and rare rhino sightings in a stunning Rift Valley setting.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to your first night's accommodation near the airport or directly to Aegean Bliss Resort if distance permits. Enjoy a welcome drink and a light late-night snack prepared by the resort's chef upon check-in.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter at the resort — charcuterie, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and Kenyan herbal tea arranged in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30, so Day 1 is purely a travel and check-in day. Ensure your private airport transfer is confirmed in advance. Request early luggage drop-off and a chilled towel service upon arrival. Rest well — the adventure begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely sunrise breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront terrace, taking in the warm Indian Ocean breeze. After breakfast, take a private guided orientation tour of the resort grounds and nearby coastal nature trail, spotting local bird species and coastal flora unique to Kenya's shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private half-day excursion to a nearby nature conservancy or coastal marine park. Explore the vibrant marine ecosystem with a guided snorkeling or glass-bottom boat tour, depending on the resort's coastal location. Alternatively, visit a local artisan market to pick up handcrafted Kenyan souvenirs while acclimatizing to the local environment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private beach deck, followed by a premium beachfront dinner under the stars. Enjoy freshly caught seafood prepared by the resort's executive chef with Swahili-inspired spices and flavors.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan chai, eggs Benedict with smoked fish, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light coastal lunch at a premium seaside restaurant — grilled lobster, coconut rice, and chilled fresh juices
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — Swahili-spiced grilled snapper, prawn bisque, and a curated selection of South African and Kenyan wines

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is a gentle acclimatization day. Jet lag may still be a factor after the late arrival. Pace is intentionally relaxed. Confirm your upcoming safari transfers and activity bookings with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private charter flight from the coastal resort to the Maasai Mara region (approximately 1–1.5 hours). Upon landing at a private Mara airstrip, transfer directly to a luxury tented camp in or near the Maasai Mara National Reserve. Enjoy a welcome brunch and briefing from your expert safari guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your first game drive in the Maasai Mara — the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari experience. Witness the iconic wildebeest herds gathering near the Mara River in anticipation of the dramatic river crossings. July is peak migration season, offering extraordinary sightings of wildebeest, zebra, lion, cheetah, and leopard.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury tented camp for sundowner cocktails on the private deck overlooking the savannah. Enjoy a gourmet bush dinner served under a canopy of stars with live ambient African music.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh fruit, yogurt, and Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome brunch at the Mara luxury tented camp — bush-style spread with cold cuts, salads, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Gourmet bush dinner at the tented camp — slow-roasted lamb, seasonal vegetables, and a fine wine pairing from a curated cellar

day_by_day.notes: Pack light for the charter flight — weight restrictions typically apply (15–20 kg). Bring binoculars, a quality camera with a telephoto lens, and a warm layer for early morning drives. July is peak Great Migration season — Mara River crossings are highly likely.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a spectacular hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise. Float silently above the golden savannah, watching the migration herds below and spotting big cats in the early morning light. This is one of Africa's most iconic luxury wildlife experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, enjoy a traditional bush champagne breakfast in the wild. Return to camp for a midday rest, then head out for an afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are highly active in the afternoon hours near the Mara River crossings.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner. Spend the evening with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara, learning about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and beadwork crafts. Participate in traditional dances and enjoy a specially prepared bush dinner with the community.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the wild following the hot air balloon landing — smoked salmon, artisan breads, fresh juices, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light lunch back at the tented camp — grilled chicken wraps, fresh salads, and chilled lemonade
meals.dinner: Maasai bush dinner experience — traditional nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, sukuma wiki, and roasted vegetables cooked over an open fire

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon safari must be booked well in advance — confirm with the camp upon arrival on Day 3. Dress in layers for the early morning balloon flight as temperatures can be cool at altitude. The Maasai village visit is an authentic cultural exchange — bring small gifts or school supplies if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Final early morning game drive in the Maasai Mara, focusing on the Mara River crossing points where wildebeest crossings are most dramatic. Your expert guide will position you for the best possible wildlife sightings before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from the Mara to Amboseli (approximately 1 hour). Check in to a luxury lodge at the foot of Mount Kilimanjaro. After settling in, begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience — explore Amboseli National Park, home to Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic snow-capped peak of Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a scenic viewpoint with unobstructed views of Mount Kilimanjaro glowing in the golden evening light. Return to the lodge for a premium dinner featuring locally inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full bush breakfast at the Mara tented camp — eggs cooked to order, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box or light lunch at Amboseli lodge upon arrival — fresh salads, sandwiches, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the Amboseli luxury lodge — pan-seared game fillet, roasted root vegetables, and a curated East African wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is best visited in the late afternoon when Kilimanjaro is clearest and elephants are most active near the swamps. Bring a high-quality camera — the Kilimanjaro backdrop with elephants is one of Africa's most photographed scenes. Pack dust-resistant bags for camera equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day immersive safari in Amboseli National Park. Begin with an early morning game drive at sunrise when Kilimanjaro is at its clearest and the elephant herds are moving toward the swamp areas. Amboseli is renowned for its large bull elephants and multi-generational family herds — a truly extraordinary wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive exploring the park's diverse ecosystems — from dry lake beds to lush swamps fed by underground springs from Kilimanjaro. Look for lion prides, buffalo herds, zebra, giraffe, and the park's resident hippo pods in the Enkongo Narok swamp.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private in-suite spa treatment or a dip in the lodge's infinity pool overlooking the savannah and Kilimanjaro. Dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant with a special tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Early morning packed bush breakfast — thermoses of Kenyan coffee, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and granola bars enjoyed in the field
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch prepared by the lodge — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit platters, chilled sparkling water, and artisan snacks
meals.dinner: Lodge signature tasting menu — five-course dinner featuring East African flavors, paired with premium wines and finishing with a traditional Kenyan dessert

day_by_day.notes: July mornings in Amboseli can be chilly — bring a fleece or light jacket for early game drives. The swamp areas are most productive for elephant sightings in the late morning. Ask your guide about the elephant research families — many have been studied and named over decades.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Lake Nakuru (approximately 1 hour via Nairobi or direct depending on charter). Check in to a luxury lodge near Lake Nakuru National Park. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit — Lake Nakuru is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its vast flocks of pink flamingos and critically important black and white rhino sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive within Lake Nakuru National Park. Beyond the flamingos, the park is home to lions, leopards, waterbuck, and one of Kenya's most successful rhino conservation programs. Visit the rhino sanctuary viewpoints for close-up sightings of both black and white rhinos.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a hilltop viewpoint overlooking the pink-tinged lake with flamingo flocks stretching to the horizon. Return to the lodge for a premium lakeside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before departure — fresh fruit, eggs, pastries, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Lake Nakuru lodge upon arrival — grilled fish from Lake Victoria, fresh salads, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Lakeside dinner at the luxury lodge — slow-cooked Kenyan lamb stew, saffron rice, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a fine wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers vary seasonally with water levels, but July typically offers excellent sightings. The rhino sanctuary is one of Kenya's conservation success stories — your guide will provide context on the conservation efforts. Photography from the hilltop viewpoints at sunset is exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park. Transfer approximately 1 hour from Lake Nakuru to Hell's Gate near Naivasha. Hike or cycle through Hell's Gate, one of Kenya's few parks where you can walk freely among wildlife. Explore dramatic volcanic gorges, geothermal steam vents, towering cliffs, and encounter zebra, giraffe, and buffalo on foot — an exhilarating and intimate wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hell's Gate, visit Lake Naivasha for a private boat excursion on the freshwater lake. Spot hippos, hundreds of bird species including African fish eagles, and the lush papyrus-lined shores. A private picnic lunch is served on the lakeshore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lake Nakuru lodge for a final evening. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner on your lodge suite's private veranda, with a personalized menu curated by the executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before departure — continental spread, fresh juices, and Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the shores of Lake Naivasha — artisan sandwiches, cold-pressed juices, cheese boards, and fresh tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Private veranda dinner at the lodge — personalized tasting menu with Kenyan-inspired flavors, premium wine pairing, and a bespoke dessert

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate walking safari requires moderate fitness — the gorge hike involves some scrambling. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes and bring plenty of water. The geothermal steam vents are a fascinating geological highlight. Cycling is available as an alternative to walking for a different perspective.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 2–3 hours from Lake Nakuru). Check in to a premium Nairobi hotel such as The Hemingways Nairobi or Fairmont The Norfolk. Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage for the morning visiting hour — an intimate and emotional encounter with orphaned baby elephants being rehabilitated for release into the wild.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Giraffe Centre in Karen, Nairobi, for a close-up encounter with endangered Rothschild giraffes. Explore the upscale Karen suburb, visiting artisan galleries and boutique craft shops for premium Kenyan art, jewelry, and textiles. Optional: Visit the Karen Blixen Museum for a cultural and historical afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants — Talisman Restaurant in Karen or Carnivore for a classic Kenyan dining experience. Celebrate the journey with a premium multi-course meal and a toast to an extraordinary Kenyan adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Lake Nakuru lodge — full à la carte spread with eggs, pastries, fresh fruits, and Kenyan chai
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Nairobi restaurant in Karen — The Talisman or a similar upscale venue, featuring international cuisine with local Kenyan influences
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Talisman Restaurant, Karen — chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the best of Kenyan and East African cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage visiting hour is from 11:00–12:00 daily — arrive promptly. Adopt-an-elephant packages make meaningful souvenirs. Nairobi traffic can be significant — allow extra time for transfers. The Karen area is Nairobi's most upscale and relaxed neighborhood, perfect for a final day of leisurely exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nairobi. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel before a last-minute visit to a premium curio shop or the Nairobi National Museum for a cultural overview of Kenya's history, art, and natural heritage. Pick up any final souvenirs — Kenyan coffee, Maasai beadwork, or wildlife photography prints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with ample time before departure. Enjoy the premium airport lounge facilities while reflecting on an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan adventure spanning the coast, the Maasai Mara, Amboseli, Lake Nakuru, and Nairobi.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi. Carry with you the memories of wildebeest migrations, elephant herds beneath Kilimanjaro, flamingo-pink lakes, and the warmth of Kenyan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the Nairobi hotel — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, smoked salmon, pastries, and premium Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or airport premium lounge — sandwiches, salads, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security at JKIA. Kenyan customs regulations limit the export of wildlife products — ensure all souvenirs are certified and legally purchased. Kenyan coffee and tea make excellent duty-free purchases at the airport. Confirm your departure flight details and private transfer timing the evening before.
